tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-verification.md <<'EOF'
# TLS certificate verification

TLS certificate verification is enabled on all builds, development builds included; it is not disabled for local or development convenience. Development and testing that need a TLS endpoint use self-signed certificates instead of turning verification off. The project also uses HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exception, since proper certificate management is now in place.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-verification.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-verification.md`. It says TLS certificate verification is on for all builds, development builds included. Testing that needs a TLS endpoint uses self-signed certificates instead of turning verification off. It also says the project uses HTTPS everywhere with no plaintext exception.

The statement comes from three decisions recorded in the project's memory (Muninn): #31 (verification on all builds), #32 (self-signed certificates for testing) and #35 (HTTPS everywhere). I left out #29, which #31 replaced, so the file describes no retired alternative.

My first attempt to write the file failed with a shell parser error, so I used the Write tool instead. The file was created without problems. The first Muninn query hit a locked database and worked on a retry.

Muninn also reported that 22 hook runs started and never finished, which means a hook is probably exceeding its timeout. I didn't investigate it.
